newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Newcrest shines on Normandy deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Newcrest shines on Normandy deal.

text.p: Shares in gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd rose nearly nine cents or nearly two percent to A$4.97 in active Friday morning trade as investors welcomed Newcrest's deal to swap its Normandy Mining Ltd stake for gold.
The deal allows Newcrest to swap its 11.9 percent stake in Normandy with ANZ Bank for 740,000 ounces of gold at A$450 an ounce to raise A$337.225 million.
Analysts and brokers said the deal allowed Newcrest to limit its loss on the Normandy stake while exposing itself to rises in the gold price and Normandy's share price.
Normandy has an option to buy back the Normandy stake from ANZ within the two years.
"The reaction's been positive," said a senior Melbourne gold analyst.

"Effectively they've bought themselves a price floor on the Normandy stake and at the same time exposed themselves to upside on the gold price and on Normandy in the event of a decent (gold price) rally," the analyst said.
Newcrest would benefit from a rise in the gold price over A$500 in particular, analysts said.
"It's a win-win situation and there's very little risk on the deal," another gold analyst said.
Brokers said the deal also allowed Newcrest to focus completely on its exploration and production activities rather than trying to offload the stake.
The Normandy shares were sold for a gold equivalent of A$1.75 per share. The company also said it would make a provision of A$134.7 million against its Normandy investment.
